$comment: Maintainer notes, stripped from the merged settings.json by install.sh, never shipped to a user's config.
Credential-read denies are conventional security defaults. They were cross-referenced against trailofbits/claude-code-config.
Nonessential-traffic env opt-outs (DISABLE_TELEMETRY et al.) live in the opt-in `telemetry-off` addition, not here, so Remote Control works by default.

Shell-rc Edit denies block the Edit-family TOOLS (the visible, approvable path — Edit(path) rules cover every file-editing tool, including Write, so a separate Write(path) rule is redundant and Claude Code's own startup validation now rejects it as dead) and stop Claude from managing your dotfiles (hand those off via `! <cmd>`). Bash-redirection writes (`echo ... >> ~/.zshrc`) are covered by command-guard.ts, which explicitly denies that vector. The two layers together close the path. Kept as a cheap defense against a persistence vector. Drop them if you want Claude editing your rc files.
